## compositionality

### From In Uselis, Dittadi and Oh's two-concept grids, ResNet-50s trained from scratch, with checkpoints chosen on the unseen pairs, reach unseen combinations as the share of combinations seen grows and not as up to four times more data of the same combinations is added; and when embeddings are exactly linearly factored, seen pairs that connect every value of both concepts, as two per value arranged in one cycle do, determine the embedding of every unseen pair

- [THEORY-117](../record/theory.d/THEORY-117.md) — In Uselis, Dittadi and Oh's two-concept grids, ResNet-50s trained from scratch, with checkpoints chosen on the unseen pairs, reach unseen combinations as the share of combinations seen grows and not as up to four times more data of the same combinations is added; and when embeddings are exactly linearly factored, seen pairs that connect every value of both concepts, as two per value arranged in one cycle do, determine the embedding of every unseen pair *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-794](../record/theory.d/THEORY-794.md) — In vision models, compositional generalization to unseen combinations of concepts is driven by the diversity of the combinations seen in training rather than by data volume, and arrives with representations that are linearly factored by concept, as Uselis, Dittadi and Oh propose *(Proposed)*

### From On the Random Hierarchy Model, in the experiments reported (s = 2, L ≤ 4, small v), deep CNNs matched to the tree and trained in a feature-learning regime reach a tenth of chance error from about n_c m^L examples, polynomial in the input dimension, at the training-set size at which their hidden layers become invariant to swapping synonymous tuples; two-layer networks and the same CNNs as fixed kernels need a number proportional to the whole input space, exponential in the input dimension, and deep CNNs stay near chance when every tuple is made equally likely in every class

  - [THEORY-786](../record/theory.d/THEORY-786.md) — Deep networks learn hierarchically generated data from a number of examples set by when the correlations between input patches and the class rise above sampling noise, so detecting those correlations is how they learn the grammar, as Cagnetta and coauthors propose *(Proposed)*

### From In the Random Hierarchy Model with v symbols per level, m rules per symbol and s-tuples, the covariance between two tokens whose lowest common ancestor is ℓ levels up has zero mean over grammars and root-mean-square size about ((1 − m/v^(s−1))/(v³ m^(2ℓ−1)))^(1/2), falling by a factor m per level, while its estimate from P sequences carries noise of about (v²P)^(−1/2), so the two meet at P_ℓ ≈ v m^(2ℓ−1)/(1 − m/v^(s−1)); all to leading order in large v and m

- [THEORY-778](../record/theory.d/THEORY-778.md) — In the Random Hierarchy Model with v symbols per level, m rules per symbol and s-tuples, the covariance between two tokens whose lowest common ancestor is ℓ levels up has zero mean over grammars and root-mean-square size about ((1 − m/v^(s−1))/(v³ m^(2ℓ−1)))^(1/2), falling by a factor m per level, while its estimate from P sequences carries noise of about (v²P)^(−1/2), so the two meet at P_ℓ ≈ v m^(2ℓ−1)/(1 − m/v^(s−1)); all to leading order in large v and m *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-201](../record/theory.d/THEORY-201.md) — In next-token prediction on hierarchically generated sequences, the correlation between two tokens falls by about a factor m per level of their common ancestor, so a training set of P sequences resolves correlations only out to a distance t*(P) at which they meet sampling noise; learners come to represent the hidden symbols up to that depth, giving loss steps at about v m^(2ℓ−1) examples, and on character-level text the context at which the loss saturates grows as P^(1/(2β)) with β the measured correlation decay *(Proposed)*

## consciousness

### From Felt affect is the experience of the body's regulatory state, valenced by what that state means for staying alive and present throughout waking experience, not only in emotion; whether what is felt is a prediction of that state or a map of it is unsettled

  - [THEORY-090](../record/theory.d/THEORY-090.md) — A basic, affective form of consciousness is realised subcortically, in the upper brainstem and thalamus, before and without cortex, and its first function is alarm: survival behaviour, care for the body and generalised one-shot learning, with no choice between options *(Proposed)*
  - [THEORY-093](../record/theory.d/THEORY-093.md) — A content of mind is conscious when a continuous flow of homeostatic feelings identifies it as the organism's own; the feelings are conscious in themselves and hybrid, partly made of the body state they map, because interoceptive pathways let the body act directly on the neurons that map it *(Proposed)*

## contextuality

### From An empirical model is Kochen–Specker-noncontextual exactly when its context distributions glue to one global distribution, and since signed global sections always exist for no-signalling models, negative probability does not mark contextuality

- [THEORY-012](../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md) — An empirical model is Kochen–Specker-noncontextual exactly when its context distributions glue to one global distribution, and since signed global sections always exist for no-signalling models, negative probability does not mark contextuality *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-011](../record/theory.d/THEORY-011.md) — Generalized contextuality is strictly broader than Kochen–Specker contextuality: a qubit already has no preparation-noncontextual model, though no Kochen–Specker argument with sharp measurements exists in dimension two *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-014](../record/theory.d/THEORY-014.md) — In both formalisms of contextuality, classicality is the existence of a nonnegative version of a linear representation that always exists over the reals, so negativity is universal and only its unavoidability is nonclassical *(Active)* — also carries further THEORY-016
  - [THEORY-015](../record/theory.d/THEORY-015.md) — Kochen–Specker noncontextuality is measurement noncontextuality plus outcome determinism for sharp measurements, and preparation noncontextuality implies that determinism, so every Kochen–Specker proof refutes universal generalized noncontextuality while measurement noncontextuality alone is consistent with quantum theory *(Active)* — also carries further THEORY-016
  - [THEORY-526](../record/theory.d/THEORY-526.md) — The Čech cohomology obstruction of a support section is a sound but incomplete witness of contextuality: it vanishes exactly when the section lies in a compatible family of integer combinations of support sections, so it is non-zero on every section of every All-vs-Nothing model, over any coefficient ring, on a connected cover, yet it misses the Hardy model entirely, part of a strongly contextual Kochen–Specker cover, and every section of a strongly contextual model on the fully symmetric (2,2,4) Bell cover *(Active)*
    - [THEORY-524](../record/theory.d/THEORY-524.md) — On cyclic measurement scenarios, where the contexts' overlaps form one chordless N-cycle, the ℤ/2 Čech obstruction computed on the (N−1)-th iterated joint model is exact for logical and strong contextuality, the bound N − 1 being tight; beyond cycles no such result is established, the published extension is false on its own example, and the completeness conjecture fails on a Kochen–Specker cover that is never detected at any level *(Active)*
- [THEORY-016](../record/theory.d/THEORY-016.md) — An operational theory admits a generalized-noncontextual model exactly when its GPT admits a positive quasiprobability representation, and for a tomographically local theory any diagram-preserving such model is an exact frame with exactly as many ontic states as the GPT's dimension *(Active)*

### From Classical Boolean logic is restored when a presheaf of contextual data acquires a global section or is sheafified

- [THEORY-024](../record/theory.d/THEORY-024.md) — Classical Boolean logic is restored when a presheaf of contextual data acquires a global section or is sheafified *(Rejected)*
  - [THEORY-516](../record/theory.d/THEORY-516.md) — For any presheaf of propositions over a small category of contexts, a sieve-valued valuation satisfies the generalized functional-composition condition exactly when it is a subobject of that presheaf, and the construction runs unchanged in classical physics, where every microstate gives a global section yet truth values are still non-Boolean sieves; so the logic of the truth values is fixed by the base category, not by whether a presheaf has global sections *(Active)*

### From In Contextuality-by-Default 2.0, whether a system of non-binary variables is contextual depends on which variables represent the measurements: coarse-graining can turn a noncontextual system into a contextual one, while for connections of two variables, and for consistently connected systems, CbD 1.0 and 2.0 agree

  - [THEORY-168](../record/theory.d/THEORY-168.md) — In Contextuality-by-Default, whether a fixed set of measurements is contextual depends on how the system is represented: which couplings are imposed, and which dichotomizations of the variables are included *(Proposed)*

### From Classical simulations between no-signalling empirical models on finite scenarios, which may change the cover, never create contextuality: a model is non-contextual exactly when the empty model simulates it, the non-contextual fraction cannot fall along a simulation, strong contextuality is reflected backwards, and only non-contextual models can be cloned

- [THEORY-720](../record/theory.d/THEORY-720.md) — Classical simulations between no-signalling empirical models on finite scenarios, which may change the cover, never create contextuality: a model is non-contextual exactly when the empty model simulates it, the non-contextual fraction cannot fall along a simulation, strong contextuality is reflected backwards, and only non-contextual models can be cloned *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-174](../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md) — Classical simulations between empirical models on different scenarios never create contextuality, and a map between model sets is such a simulation exactly when a non-contextual model of the hom scenario induces it *(Proposed)*

## databases

### From When stored views are never updated, greedily storing the view of largest marginal saving in query cost gets at least 1 − 1/e of the optimal saving on a data-cube lattice or any OR or AND view graph, against the optimum for the same number of views or for the space the greedy ends up using, which may exceed the budget by one view

  - [THEORY-350](../record/theory.d/THEORY-350.md) — Under a budget on maintenance time, a stored view's upkeep depends on which other views are stored, so upkeep is not additive and adding a view can lower it, and greedily adding the single view of best saving per unit of upkeep can be arbitrarily bad; on OR view graphs a greedy over inverted tree sets gets 1 − 1/e of the saving of an optimum given as much upkeep, using up to twice the budget, if no tree-piece of the optimum alone exceeds the budget *(Active)*

### From Locality-sensitive hashing answers approximate near-neighbour queries over n points with O(n^ρ) hash evaluations in O(dn + n^{1+ρ}) space, where ρ = ln(1/p1)/ln(1/p2) is set by how much more often near pairs collide than far ones and is at most 1/(1+ε) for approximation 1+ε in Hamming space, with constant success probability per query; the paper gives upper bounds only and proves no limit on what organizing can buy

- [THEORY-388](../record/theory.d/THEORY-388.md) — Locality-sensitive hashing answers approximate near-neighbour queries over n points with O(n^ρ) hash evaluations in O(dn + n^{1+ρ}) space, where ρ = ln(1/p1)/ln(1/p2) is set by how much more often near pairs collide than far ones and is at most 1/(1+ε) for approximation 1+ε in Hamming space, with constant success probability per query; the paper gives upper bounds only and proves no limit on what organizing can buy *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-372](../record/theory.d/THEORY-372.md) — For c-approximate near-neighbour search over n points in Euclidean space, space n^{1+ρu+o(1)} and query time n^{ρq+o(1)} are achievable on any data set whenever c²√ρq + (c²−1)√ρu ≥ √(2c²−1) (c√ρq + (c−1)√ρu ≥ √(2c−1) in Hamming space), and no list-of-points structure, the model of known data-independent hashing, does better on random instances; without that model the curve is matched only at query time n^{o(1)} by one or two cell probes *(Active)*

### From For positive relational algebra on relations whose tuples are annotated from a commutative semiring, every query's annotated answer equals its answer over provenance polynomials N[X] in the input tuple ids, evaluated at the input annotations, so set, bag, c-table and event-table semantics all factor through the polynomials; revaluing inputs can remove output tuples but never add them, and nothing is shown for negation, difference or aggregation

  - [THEORY-380](../record/theory.d/THEORY-380.md) — For datalog over a finite input instance annotated from a commutative ω-continuous semiring, with an answer's tag defined as the sum over its derivation trees of the product of its leaves' tags, the tags are the least fixed point of a finite polynomial system and factor through formal power series N∞⟦X⟧ in the input tuple ids; an answer tuple's series has an infinite coefficient exactly when one of its derivation trees contains a tuple lying on a cycle of unit rules *(Active)*

### From When a cached interval of width W is kept valid by its source, which pushes a refresh at cost C_vr whenever the value leaves it, and queries fetch the exact value at cost C_qr whenever it is too wide, and the chances of the two per step go as 1/W² and as W, the expected refresh cost is least at W* = (ρK₁/K₂)^(1/3) with ρ = 2C_vr/C_qr, where ρ times the chance of a pushed refresh equals the chance of a fetch

- [THEORY-386](../record/theory.d/THEORY-386.md) — When a cached interval of width W is kept valid by its source, which pushes a refresh at cost C_vr whenever the value leaves it, and queries fetch the exact value at cost C_qr whenever it is too wide, and the chances of the two per step go as 1/W² and as W, the expected refresh cost is least at W* = (ρK₁/K₂)^(1/3) with ρ = 2C_vr/C_qr, where ρ times the chance of a pushed refresh equals the chance of a fetch *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-377](../record/theory.d/THEORY-377.md) — In Olston, Loo and Widom's simulations, a rule that multiplies a cached interval's width by 1 + α on a pushed refresh with probability min{ρ, 1}, and divides it by 1 + α on a query's exact fetch with probability min{1/ρ, 1}, settled within 1% of the best fixed width on one random walk and within 5% over eight walk settings; on a 50-host network-traffic trace, restricted to exact copies, it almost matched a tuned adaptive cache-or-not rule, and with a 50-value cache, where queries tolerated imprecision, it cost less; that it converges to the best width is argued, not proved *(Active)*

  - [THEORY-093](../record/theory.d/THEORY-093.md) — A content of mind is conscious when a continuous flow of homeostatic feelings identifies it as the organism's own; the feelings are conscious in themselves and hybrid, partly made of the body state they map, because interoceptive pathways let the body act directly on the neurons that map it *(Proposed)*

## epistemology

### From When a group learns only about the options its members pursue and good evidence is scarce, sparser communication makes it more likely to settle on the better option, at a large cost in speed; when evidence is plentiful, sparsity only slows learning

  - [THEORY-148](../record/theory.d/THEORY-148.md) — A group learning by trying needs diversity in what its members pursue that lasts long enough to survive misleading early evidence and then gives way to consensus; limited communication and stubborn priors each supply it, and together they make it permanent, so the group never settles *(Proposed)*
  - [THEORY-422](../record/theory.d/THEORY-422.md) — In the standard formal models of group learning, no communication network is best for every epistemic problem: costly transmission favours minimally connected or star networks, pooling of estimates by averaging favours regular networks, and learning by trying in bandit problems can favour sparse ones, so a group's network cannot be judged until its learning problem is known *(Active)*

### From On the court agenda {P, Q, R, R iff (P and Q)} under universal domain, proposition-wise majority voting is not robustly rational, while the premise-based procedure is, and it makes the group's judgments a function of the members' whole judgment sets that the members' judgments on the conclusion neither fix nor need to enter

## loss-landscapes

### From Linear connectivity from a shared, already-stable start holds only when the objectives the runs optimise share structure, and breaks as that structure is removed

  - [THEORY-105](../record/theory.d/THEORY-105.md) — Fine-tuning from one pretrained model lands near the edge of a task-specific low-loss region that contains the convex hull of the fine-tuned models, and averaging them moves inward *(Proposed)*

### From Two ε-dropout-stable solutions of a multilayer ReLU net, under a loss convex in the output, are joined by a piecewise-linear path whose loss never exceeds the worse endpoint's by more than ε, and joined pairwise paths compose with no higher barrier than their worst

- [THEORY-736](../record/theory.d/THEORY-736.md) — Two ε-dropout-stable solutions of a multilayer ReLU net, under a loss convex in the output, are joined by a piecewise-linear path whose loss never exceeds the worse endpoint's by more than ε, and joined pairwise paths compose with no higher barrier than their worst *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-109](../record/theory.d/THEORY-109.md) — The solutions SGD finds in a deep network lie in one connected low-loss set, joined by simple curves and spanning volumes of measurable dimension, and this is a property of the solutions training finds, not of every minimum *(Proposed)*
    - [THEORY-112](../record/theory.d/THEORY-112.md) — Once the architecture's symmetries are factored out, most of the linear barrier between independently trained solutions disappears; the group that matters is the full one, permutations for MLPs and CNNs but for transformers also an orthogonal map on the residual stream, without which a barrier remains; and the barrier left after alignment falls with width and rises with depth *(Proposed)*
      - [THEORY-110](../record/theory.d/THEORY-110.md) — A set of trained solutions has a centre that is linearly connected, after alignment, to the rest of them: the solution set is a star domain even where it is not convex *(Proposed)* — also carries further THEORY-109, THEORY-741
    - [THEORY-114](../record/theory.d/THEORY-114.md) — Linear mode connectivity emerges during training, not at initialization: copies trained from a shared state become stable to SGD noise after 1.5–20% of training, and independently trained networks become linearly connected after alignment only gradually *(Proposed)*
    - [THEORY-557](../record/theory.d/THEORY-557.md) — Low-loss paths between independently trained solutions are found outside supervised image classifiers: graph neural networks trained from different seeds on one graph are joined by quadratic Bezier curves where the straight line has a barrier, and one pair each of diffusion and contrastive models by chains of low-loss checkpoints *(Proposed)*
- [THEORY-741](../record/theory.d/THEORY-741.md) — A two-layer ReLU student of width at least kM, fitting an orthonormal teacher of M neurons on the sphere, has for any k global minima a global minimum joined to each by a two-piece linear path of minima; and in a deep linear network of depth L and width above 1 + r(L − 1), any r global minima in general position share a global minimum linearly connected to each *(Active)*

### From A linear barrier between two minima that survives the removal of symmetries marks a difference in the input attributes the two models rely on: they compute by different mechanisms

  - [THEORY-111](../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md) — Along a low-loss linear path between two networks, every layer's features are the interpolation of the endpoints' features, so averaging weights within a basin averages features *(Proposed)* — also carries further THEORY-732
- [THEORY-732](../record/theory.d/THEORY-732.md) — For ReLU networks interpolated linearly between two endpoints, weak additivity and commutativity at every layer make each layer's features exactly the interpolation of the endpoints' features, output-layer linearity bounds the path's error by twice the endpoints', and for one hidden layer with interpolating minima linear mode connectivity alone gives the exact case *(Active)*

### From In Kunin et al.'s underdamped Langevin model of SGD with momentum on linear regression, with gradient-noise covariance σ²H independent of the parameters, the stationary state is Gaussian with parameter covariance ησ²H(H + λI)⁻¹/(2S(1 − β)) and velocity covariance σ²H/(S(1 − β²)): for small weight decay it spreads equally along every nonzero Hessian direction and not along the null space, each Hessian eigenmode is a damped oscillator with damping ratio (1 − β)/√(2η(1 + β)(ρ + λ)), and the expected squared step is η²σ² tr(H)/(S(1 − β²))

- [THEORY-779](../record/theory.d/THEORY-779.md) — In Kunin et al.'s underdamped Langevin model of SGD with momentum on linear regression, with gradient-noise covariance σ²H independent of the parameters, the stationary state is Gaussian with parameter covariance ησ²H(H + λI)⁻¹/(2S(1 − β)) and velocity covariance σ²H/(S(1 − β²)): for small weight decay it spreads equally along every nonzero Hessian direction and not along the null space, each Hessian eigenmode is a damped oscillator with damping ratio (1 − β)/√(2η(1 + β)(ρ + λ)), and the expected squared step is η²σ² tr(H)/(S(1 − β²)) *(Active)*

### From In the stochastic-differential-equation model of SGD, with a gradient-noise covariance that depends on the parameters, minibatch noise drives the difference of squared norms along a rescaling symmetry, at a rate proportional to learning rate over batch size, to the point on the symmetry orbit where the gradient-noise traces of the two parameter groups are equal, whenever both groups carry noise; so at stationarity SGD neither keeps the difference fixed, as gradient flow does, nor lets it diffuse, as isotropic noise does, and differs from gradient descent by a finite amount however small the noise

  - [THEORY-790](../record/theory.d/THEORY-790.md) — In deep networks trained by SGD on real data, minibatch noise drives parameter groups related by a rescaling symmetry toward the point where their gradient noise balances, at a rate set by learning rate over batch size, so that at stationarity they sit neither where gradient flow would leave them nor spread out as under isotropic noise, as Ziyin, Li and Ueda propose *(Proposed)*

### From Every mirror symmetry of a network's per-sample loss makes its symmetric subspace invariant under gradient descent and SGD, and when the loss's Hessian is bounded below by −c, weight decay γ‖θ‖² with γ > c/2 puts every minimum in that subspace; rescaling symmetries that hold at λ = −1, rotation symmetries and permutation symmetries contain such mirrors, whose subspaces are zeroed weights, reduced rank and identical neurons

### From Under MSE loss, in Han, Papyan and Donoho's VGG, ResNet and DenseNet runs on five balanced ten-class datasets, the trained classifier stays near the least-squares classifier for its own features from an early epoch; and on that central path, for unconstrained features continually renormalized to identity within-class covariance and without weight decay, gradient flow drives the class-separation singular values to infinity at equal rates, which in that model is neural collapse

  - [THEORY-797](../record/theory.d/THEORY-797.md) — Deep classifiers trained with MSE loss stay near the least-squares classifier for their own features and move along the central path by the dynamics of continually renormalized gradient flow, whose equal-rate growth of the whitened class-separation singular values is how they reach neural collapse, as Han, Papyan and Donoho propose *(Proposed)*

### From Recovery of a k-sparse vector by ℓ₁ minimization from n random measurements in dimension N switches, as N grows with δ = n/N and ρ = k/n fixed, from near-certain success to near-certain failure across a curve ρ(δ) that, for Gaussian matrices, the authors' earlier face-counting theorems fix; in 2,948,000 optimizations at N = 200, 400 and 1600, eight non-Gaussian ensembles approached that curve in a way consistent with gaps shrinking as N^(−1/2), an exponent fitted on the same data, while at finite N the location depended on the ensemble

### From In a one-locus model with non-overlapping generations, random mating and weak selection, gene frequencies change as if each individual maximized its inclusive fitness, so a trait that costs its bearer spreads only if its effect on relatives exceeds 1/r times the cost; the increase of mean inclusive fitness is proved only for traits whose total effect on others is not negative

  - [THEORY-655](../record/theory.d/THEORY-655.md) — Social behaviour evolves as if each individual valued a neighbour's fitness against its own by their coefficient of relationship, and its discriminations evolve to make that coefficient determinate; so kin are favoured and strangers met with hostility, relatives fight less, and haplodiploid sisters, related by 3/4, are predisposed to worker altruism *(Proposed)*
- [THEORY-672](../record/theory.d/THEORY-672.md) — In the iterated Prisoner's Dilemma with a probability w of meeting again, no strategy does better against an established TIT FOR TAT than TIT FOR TAT does against itself if and only if w ≥ (T−R)/(T−P) and w ≥ (T−R)/(R−S); always defecting is stable for every w, a cluster of reciprocators can invade it, and a nice stable strategy resists clusters, but the stability is only neutral, since always cooperating ties *(Active)*

  - [THEORY-673](../record/theory.d/THEORY-673.md) — The Price equation follows from any ancestor–descendant mapping in a closed population and is, like f = ma, a generalization-sketch: a schema that is empty of predictions until a specific model supplies entities, characters, time step and causes, whose value lies in unifying and guiding model construction, so the charges that it is a tautology or lacks predictive power and dynamic sufficiency ask of it what only its specialisations can supply *(Proposed)*

## philosophy-of-language

### From To mean something by an utterance, in the non-natural sense, is to intend it to produce an effect in an audience by means of the audience's recognition of that intention, where the recognition is meant to be a reason for the effect and not merely its cause; an intention to produce the effect, or to have it recognised, is not enough

- [THEORY-444](../record/theory.d/THEORY-444.md) — To mean something by an utterance, in the non-natural sense, is to intend it to produce an effect in an audience by means of the audience's recognition of that intention, where the recognition is meant to be a reason for the effect and not merely its cause; an intention to produce the effect, or to have it recognised, is not enough *(Proposed)*
  - [THEORY-511](../record/theory.d/THEORY-511.md) — Illocutionary acts that are not essentially conventional, such as warning, entreating and objecting, are individuated by a wholly overt, audience-directed intention, Grice's three intentions with a fourth that the audience recognise the second, and are performed when that intention is understood; acts such as verdicts and umpires' calls exist only within rule-governed procedures and fall outside the scheme *(Proposed)*

## philosophy-of-mathematics

### From An adjunction between a category and the opposite of another restricts to a dual equivalence between the full subcategories on which its unit and counit are isomorphisms

- [THEORY-729](../record/theory.d/THEORY-729.md) — An adjunction between a category and the opposite of another restricts to a dual equivalence between the full subcategories on which its unit and counit are isomorphisms *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-604](../record/theory.d/THEORY-604.md) — Most mathematical dualities are adjunctions between one category and the opposite of another, which become dual equivalences on their fixed points; what makes them dualities rather than equivalences is the reversal of arrows, so many of the 'dualities' physicists name are, in the mathematician's sense, equivalences or symmetries *(Proposed)*

## philosophy-of-science

### From A Markov-blanket partition is defined relative to a chosen internal set, so a graph has one around almost any set of nodes, and the formalism alone does not say which set is the system

- [THEORY-066](../record/theory.d/THEORY-066.md) — A Markov-blanket partition is defined relative to a chosen internal set, so a graph has one around almost any set of nodes, and the formalism alone does not say which set is the system *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-073](../record/theory.d/THEORY-073.md) — A Markov blanket does not individuate a system: where it falls is fixed by modelling choices made before it is found, so it presupposes the boundary it is used to find, and it cannot represent a boundary the system produces *(Proposed)*

### From When a group learns only about the options its members pursue and good evidence is scarce, sparser communication makes it more likely to settle on the better option, at a large cost in speed; when evidence is plentiful, sparsity only slows learning

- [THEORY-143](../record/theory.d/THEORY-143.md) — When a group learns only about the options its members pursue and good evidence is scarce, sparser communication makes it more likely to settle on the better option, at a large cost in speed; when evidence is plentiful, sparsity only slows learning *(Proposed)*
  - [THEORY-148](../record/theory.d/THEORY-148.md) — A group learning by trying needs diversity in what its members pursue that lasts long enough to survive misleading early evidence and then gives way to consensus; limited communication and stubborn priors each supply it, and together they make it permanent, so the group never settles *(Proposed)*
  - [THEORY-422](../record/theory.d/THEORY-422.md) — In the standard formal models of group learning, no communication network is best for every epistemic problem: costly transmission favours minimally connected or star networks, pooling of estimates by averaging favours regular networks, and learning by trying in bandit problems can favour sparse ones, so a group's network cannot be judged until its learning problem is known *(Active)*

### From In the three-unit identity network x ↦ x(1, 0, 1) ↦ (0, 2, 1)·h, aligning the input with the third unit and aligning it with the direction (h₁ + h₂)/√2, two alignments related by an orthogonal change of basis, pass every interchange intervention on the input equally, so interchange interventions on that variable alone do not fix which internal direction mediates it

- [THEORY-243](../record/theory.d/THEORY-243.md) — In the three-unit identity network x ↦ x(1, 0, 1) ↦ (0, 2, 1)·h, aligning the input with the third unit and aligning it with the direction (h₁ + h₂)/√2, two alignments related by an orthogonal change of basis, pass every interchange intervention on the input equally, so interchange interventions on that variable alone do not fix which internal direction mediates it *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-802](../record/theory.d/THEORY-802.md) — In trained networks as in constructed ones, interchange interventions on a fixed set of variables can be satisfied equally by alignments related by a change of basis, so which internal direction mediates a high-level variable is fixed only relative to a chosen decomposition into units, and complex models will generally have several distinct, fully correct abstractions *(Proposed)*

### From In a community whose consensus model is replaced whenever a single sound pairwise model comparison favours the challenger, which models get proposed can hold the consensus on a false model while results reproduce almost perfectly, so reproducibility need not track convergence to truth

- [THEORY-295](../record/theory.d/THEORY-295.md) — In a community whose consensus model is replaced whenever a single sound pairwise model comparison favours the challenger, which models get proposed can hold the consensus on a false model while results reproduce almost perfectly, so reproducibility need not track convergence to truth *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-814](../record/theory.d/THEORY-814.md) — In scientific communities that settle on a consensus model by sound model comparisons, high reproducibility of results is not evidence that the consensus is true, because which alternatives get proposed can hold a false consensus whose results reproduce almost perfectly *(Proposed)*

### From In Garg and Fetzer's GPT-4o-mini extraction from NBER and CEPR working papers, edges kept in at least 4 of 9 passes and never checked against human labels, the mean per-paper share of edges labelled as backed by difference-in-differences, instrumental variables, an RCT, regression discontinuity or synthetic control rose from 7.7% in 1990 to 31.7% in 2020, at every overlap threshold; the paper's per-decade slope fell from +0.0187 to +0.0011 once method mix and graph volume were controlled

- [THEORY-674](../record/theory.d/THEORY-674.md) — In Garg and Fetzer's GPT-4o-mini extraction from NBER and CEPR working papers, edges kept in at least 4 of 9 passes and never checked against human labels, the mean per-paper share of edges labelled as backed by difference-in-differences, instrumental variables, an RCT, regression discontinuity or synthetic control rose from 7.7% in 1990 to 31.7% in 2020, at every overlap threshold; the paper's per-decade slope fell from +0.0187 to +0.0011 once method mix and graph volume were controlled *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-824](../record/theory.d/THEORY-824.md) — Economics working papers increasingly back their claims with design-based identification: in NBER and CEPR working papers the share of claims supported by difference-in-differences, instrumental variables, an RCT, regression discontinuity or synthetic control rose about fourfold from 1990 to 2020 *(Proposed)*

## pragmatics

### From A speaker who chooses words to minimise the information lost about a single intended referent, with words' literal meanings uniform over their extensions, picks each true word with probability inversely proportional to a power of its extension, so the size principle follows from informative communication; in one betting experiment, learners who knew the referent bet on a novel word's meaning in line with the inversion of that speaker (r = .93 on condition means), and in one free-description study speakers' word use followed it only weakly (r = .19)

- [THEORY-472](../record/theory.d/THEORY-472.md) — A speaker who chooses words to minimise the information lost about a single intended referent, with words' literal meanings uniform over their extensions, picks each true word with probability inversely proportional to a power of its extension, so the size principle follows from informative communication; in one betting experiment, learners who knew the referent bet on a novel word's meaning in line with the inversion of that speaker (r = .93 on condition means), and in one free-description study speakers' word use followed it only weakly (r = .19) *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-172](../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md) — In Frank and Goodman's one-shot reference games, listeners' mean bets matched a parameter-free listener inverting a speaker who chooses among true utterances by informativeness, with a separately measured salience prior, and not salience alone; and in Bergen, Goodman and Levy's signalling games with novel symbols, listeners read a signal as excluding what the available alternative would have conveyed *(Active)*
    - [THEORY-785](../record/theory.d/THEORY-785.md) — Listeners interpret an utterance by inverting a model of a speaker who chooses among alternatives by informativeness, so what a fixed form conveys depends on what else the speaker could have said, as the rational speech act account of Frank, Goodman and coauthors proposes *(Proposed)*
  - [THEORY-816](../record/theory.d/THEORY-816.md) — Learners inferring what a novel word means from its use reason about a speaker who chose the word to be informative about the referent, so the size principle in word learning is a consequence of that inference and not a separate rule of generalisation *(Proposed)*

### From When a sequence generator's latent dynamics factor as a tensor product, its predictive state embeds losslessly and linearly in orthogonal per-factor subspaces of total dimension Σ(d_n − 1); 4-layer GPT-2-style transformers trained by next-token prediction on five Mess3 and Bloch Walk factors settle near that dimension, in per-factor subspaces that are linearly independent and approximately orthogonal in their leading components, and under the token noise tested reach it first even when noise makes it lossy

### From MSN's objective penalizes unequal cluster sizes explicitly and SwAV's enforces equal sizes, and in one study with mini-batches of two to eight ImageNet classes, SimCLR, MSN and VICReg lost 11 to 18 points of ImageNet linear accuracy while MAE and data2vec lost under one

- [THEORY-306](../record/theory.d/THEORY-306.md) — MSN's objective penalizes unequal cluster sizes explicitly and SwAV's enforces equal sizes, and in one study with mini-batches of two to eight ImageNet classes, SimCLR, MSN and VICReg lost 11 to 18 points of ImageNet linear accuracy while MAE and data2vec lost under one *(Active)*

### From With a kernel normalised to k(x,x) = 1, the covariance operator of a distribution is a density operator, and its quantum relative entropy is a lower bound on the Kullback–Leibler divergence that is tight for every pair of distributions only for an orthonormal, hence discrete, embedding, lies above the KL of the kernel-smoothed distributions, and on the torus, with Fourier coefficients proportional to e^(−σ‖ω‖₁) and strictly positive Lipschitz densities, is within O(σ²) of KL as the bandwidth σ shrinks

- [THEORY-313](../record/theory.d/THEORY-313.md) — With a kernel normalised to k(x,x) = 1, the covariance operator of a distribution is a density operator, and its quantum relative entropy is a lower bound on the Kullback–Leibler divergence that is tight for every pair of distributions only for an orthonormal, hence discrete, embedding, lies above the KL of the kernel-smoothed distributions, and on the torus, with Fourier coefficients proportional to e^(−σ‖ω‖₁) and strictly positive Lipschitz densities, is within O(σ²) of KL as the bandwidth σ shrinks *(Active)*

### From For binary outcomes and a fixed representation of individuals, a predictor can pass every test in a bounded class without being close to nature: outcome indistinguishability to tests that see the sampled prediction is equivalent, with stated losses, to multicalibration over a closely related class of sets, a predictor meeting it exists at size polynomial in the tests' size and the tolerance whatever nature's complexity, and learning one is as hard as weak agnostic learning of the class

- [THEORY-349](../record/theory.d/THEORY-349.md) — For binary outcomes and a fixed representation of individuals, a predictor can pass every test in a bounded class without being close to nature: outcome indistinguishability to tests that see the sampled prediction is equivalent, with stated losses, to multicalibration over a closely related class of sets, a predictor meeting it exists at size polynomial in the tests' size and the tolerance whatever nature's complexity, and learning one is as hard as weak agnostic learning of the class *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-354](../record/theory.d/THEORY-354.md) — An observer's power to refute a predictor depends on its access to the predictor as well as on its budget: against tests that see only the sampled prediction a predictor of size O(s/ε²) always passes, but if fine-grained clique counting is hard, or BPP ≠ PSPACE, some cheap tests that may query the predictor adaptively pass only predictors about as costly as nature's own *(Active)*

## quantum-foundations

### From An empirical model is Kochen–Specker-noncontextual exactly when its context distributions glue to one global distribution, and since signed global sections always exist for no-signalling models, negative probability does not mark contextuality

- [THEORY-012](../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md) — An empirical model is Kochen–Specker-noncontextual exactly when its context distributions glue to one global distribution, and since signed global sections always exist for no-signalling models, negative probability does not mark contextuality *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-011](../record/theory.d/THEORY-011.md) — Generalized contextuality is strictly broader than Kochen–Specker contextuality: a qubit already has no preparation-noncontextual model, though no Kochen–Specker argument with sharp measurements exists in dimension two *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-014](../record/theory.d/THEORY-014.md) — In both formalisms of contextuality, classicality is the existence of a nonnegative version of a linear representation that always exists over the reals, so negativity is universal and only its unavoidability is nonclassical *(Active)* — also carries further THEORY-016
  - [THEORY-015](../record/theory.d/THEORY-015.md) — Kochen–Specker noncontextuality is measurement noncontextuality plus outcome determinism for sharp measurements, and preparation noncontextuality implies that determinism, so every Kochen–Specker proof refutes universal generalized noncontextuality while measurement noncontextuality alone is consistent with quantum theory *(Active)* — also carries further THEORY-016
  - [THEORY-526](../record/theory.d/THEORY-526.md) — The Čech cohomology obstruction of a support section is a sound but incomplete witness of contextuality: it vanishes exactly when the section lies in a compatible family of integer combinations of support sections, so it is non-zero on every section of every All-vs-Nothing model, over any coefficient ring, on a connected cover, yet it misses the Hardy model entirely, part of a strongly contextual Kochen–Specker cover, and every section of a strongly contextual model on the fully symmetric (2,2,4) Bell cover *(Active)*
    - [THEORY-524](../record/theory.d/THEORY-524.md) — On cyclic measurement scenarios, where the contexts' overlaps form one chordless N-cycle, the ℤ/2 Čech obstruction computed on the (N−1)-th iterated joint model is exact for logical and strong contextuality, the bound N − 1 being tight; beyond cycles no such result is established, the published extension is false on its own example, and the completeness conjecture fails on a Kochen–Specker cover that is never detected at any level *(Active)*
- [THEORY-016](../record/theory.d/THEORY-016.md) — An operational theory admits a generalized-noncontextual model exactly when its GPT admits a positive quasiprobability representation, and for a tomographically local theory any diagram-preserving such model is an exact frame with exactly as many ontic states as the GPT's dimension *(Active)*

### From Classical Boolean logic is restored when a presheaf of contextual data acquires a global section or is sheafified

- [THEORY-024](../record/theory.d/THEORY-024.md) — Classical Boolean logic is restored when a presheaf of contextual data acquires a global section or is sheafified *(Rejected)*
  - [THEORY-516](../record/theory.d/THEORY-516.md) — For any presheaf of propositions over a small category of contexts, a sieve-valued valuation satisfies the generalized functional-composition condition exactly when it is a subobject of that presheaf, and the construction runs unchanged in classical physics, where every microstate gives a global section yet truth values are still non-Boolean sieves; so the logic of the truth values is fixed by the base category, not by whether a presheaf has global sections *(Active)*

### From Classical simulations between no-signalling empirical models on finite scenarios, which may change the cover, never create contextuality: a model is non-contextual exactly when the empty model simulates it, the non-contextual fraction cannot fall along a simulation, strong contextuality is reflected backwards, and only non-contextual models can be cloned

- [THEORY-720](../record/theory.d/THEORY-720.md) — Classical simulations between no-signalling empirical models on finite scenarios, which may change the cover, never create contextuality: a model is non-contextual exactly when the empty model simulates it, the non-contextual fraction cannot fall along a simulation, strong contextuality is reflected backwards, and only non-contextual models can be cloned *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-174](../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md) — Classical simulations between empirical models on different scenarios never create contextuality, and a map between model sets is such a simulation exactly when a non-contextual model of the hom scenario induces it *(Proposed)*

### From In Aerts's subspace model of Hampton's membership data, and in any lattice whose membership weight is order-preserving, whatever its negation, taking concept conjunction and disjunction as meet and join cannot produce overextension or underextension, so a model of the guppy-type deviations must take conjunction as some operation other than the meet or drop the monotone weight, while the Kolmogorov-type deviations can be had from the meet of a non-Boolean subspace lattice

- [THEORY-255](../record/theory.d/THEORY-255.md) — In Aerts's subspace model of Hampton's membership data, and in any lattice whose membership weight is order-preserving, whatever its negation, taking concept conjunction and disjunction as meet and join cannot produce overextension or underextension, so a model of the guppy-type deviations must take conjunction as some operation other than the meet or drop the monotone weight, while the Kolmogorov-type deviations can be had from the meet of a non-Boolean subspace lattice *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-807](../record/theory.d/THEORY-807.md) — The guppy-type overextension in Hampton's membership data arises because a combined concept is in part a new, emergent concept and not only a logical combination of its parts, so human concept combination runs in two superposed layers, one classical and logical and one quantum and conceptual *(Proposed)*

## representation-learning

### From On a finite augmentation space, over unconstrained functions of the two views, the spectral contrastive and NT-Logistic losses are both minimized at the positive-pair density ratio

- [THEORY-719](../record/theory.d/THEORY-719.md) — On a finite augmentation space, over unconstrained functions of the two views, the spectral contrastive and NT-Logistic losses are both minimized at the positive-pair density ratio *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-001](../record/theory.d/THEORY-001.md) — On a finite augmentation space, InfoNCE, logistic and spectral contrastive losses share one population optimum: the positive-pair density ratio *(Proposed)*
    - [THEORY-007](../record/theory.d/THEORY-007.md) — Kernel PCA under the positive-pair density ratio recovers the eigenfunctions of the positive-pair Markov chain, and their top span is minimax-optimal for linear prediction of approximately view-invariant targets *(Active)*
      - [THEORY-005](../record/theory.d/THEORY-005.md) — The positive-pair density ratio is the kernel of the conditional-expectation operator on L²(p), so spectral representations are that operator's eigenfunctions, well defined when the positive-pair χ²-divergence is finite *(Proposed)*
      - [THEORY-009](../record/theory.d/THEORY-009.md) — In the positive-pair spectral self-supervised papers, self-adjointness comes from the symmetry of the positive-pair distribution, not from the Riesz representation theorem; elsewhere in the family it comes from a symmetrized loss, a precondition on the kernel, or composing the conditional-expectation operator with its adjoint *(Active)*

### From For the final embedding and unembedding of a softmax model, the output distribution fixes the representations only up to an invertible linear map, and whether closeness in distribution bounds representational dissimilarity depends on the distance: not for KL in the saturation regime, but yes for the log-likelihood variance distance

  - [THEORY-002](../record/theory.d/THEORY-002.md) — Convergence of representations, in the Platonic hypothesis's sense, is convergence of kernels, which fixes representations only up to the symmetry group of what is observed; whether closeness in distribution implies closeness of representation depends on the distance used *(Proposed)*

### From In Papyan, Han and Donoho's runs of VGG, ResNet and DenseNet trained with cross-entropy on seven balanced datasets without augmentation, training past zero error shrinks last-layer within-class variability against between-class variability, and moves the centred class means and the classifier toward a common simplex equiangular tight frame and the decision toward nearest class mean, nearly to completion on the four easier datasets and only partly on ImageNet

  - [THEORY-111](../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md) — Along a low-loss linear path between two networks, every layer's features are the interpolation of the endpoints' features, so averaging weights within a basin averages features *(Proposed)* — also carries further THEORY-732
- [THEORY-732](../record/theory.d/THEORY-732.md) — For ReLU networks interpolated linearly between two endpoints, weak additivity and commutativity at every layer make each layer's features exactly the interpolation of the endpoints' features, output-layer linearity bounds the path's error by twice the endpoints', and for one hidden layer with interpolating minima linear mode connectivity alone gives the exact case *(Active)*

### From In Uselis, Dittadi and Oh's two-concept grids, ResNet-50s trained from scratch, with checkpoints chosen on the unseen pairs, reach unseen combinations as the share of combinations seen grows and not as up to four times more data of the same combinations is added; and when embeddings are exactly linearly factored, seen pairs that connect every value of both concepts, as two per value arranged in one cycle do, determine the embedding of every unseen pair

  - [THEORY-127](../record/theory.d/THEORY-127.md) — On the court agenda, and on any agenda in which every proposition reaches every other by conditional entailment and some minimally inconsistent triple stays consistent with two of its members negated, a group whose judgments are robustly rational under universal domain and respect unanimity cannot form its judgment on each proposition from its members' judgments on that proposition alone unless one member dictates; its judgments must supervene on the members' whole sets of judgments, and so can depart from what the members judge on the same proposition while being wholly fixed by them *(Active)*

### From A platform that sits between the two sides of a market and can cheaply change how it allocates value tends to decay in three stages, first good to its users, then abusing them to favour its business customers, then abusing both to claw the value back for itself, each stage made possible by the lock-in the one before it built; how far it can go is set by the cost of leaving, so lowering that cost is the remedy

- [THEORY-150](../record/theory.d/THEORY-150.md) — A platform that sits between the two sides of a market and can cheaply change how it allocates value tends to decay in three stages, first good to its users, then abusing them to favour its business customers, then abusing both to claw the value back for itself, each stage made possible by the lock-in the one before it built; how far it can go is set by the cost of leaving, so lowering that cost is the remedy *(Proposed)*
  - [THEORY-470](../record/theory.d/THEORY-470.md) — Platform decay of the enshittification kind is caused not by a change in the character of those who run platforms but by the weakening of four constraints that used to discipline them, competition, regulation, interoperability and the bargaining power of tech workers, so it is reversible if those constraints are durably restored *(Proposed)*

## thermodynamics

### From For a system driven without feedback through fixed kernels, the average work dissipated at each switch of the drive equals the memory that fails to predict the next input; that is nonnegative when the drive is Markov and, summed, bounds the protocol's dissipation from below when each kernel keeps its equilibrium stationary, so there only nonpredictive memory is wasteful; with feedback, in one binary channel no predictive agent is efficient

- [THEORY-026](../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md) — For a system driven without feedback through fixed kernels, the average work dissipated at each switch of the drive equals the memory that fails to predict the next input; that is nonnegative when the drive is Markov and, summed, bounds the protocol's dissipation from below when each kernel keeps its equilibrium stationary, so there only nonpredictive memory is wasteful; with feedback, in one binary channel no predictive agent is efficient *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-817](../record/theory.d/THEORY-817.md) — Once an agent's actions affect the percepts it receives, maximal prediction of those percepts is generally not what thermodynamic efficiency requires: in percept-action loops with feedback, maximally predictive agents generally extract less work than the most efficient agent *(Proposed)*

### From In Kunin et al.'s underdamped Langevin model of SGD with momentum on linear regression, with gradient-noise covariance σ²H independent of the parameters, the stationary state is Gaussian with parameter covariance ησ²H(H + λI)⁻¹/(2S(1 − β)) and velocity covariance σ²H/(S(1 − β²)): for small weight decay it spreads equally along every nonzero Hessian direction and not along the null space, each Hessian eigenmode is a damped oscillator with damping ratio (1 − β)/√(2η(1 + β)(ρ + λ)), and the expected squared step is η²σ² tr(H)/(S(1 − β²))

- [THEORY-779](../record/theory.d/THEORY-779.md) — In Kunin et al.'s underdamped Langevin model of SGD with momentum on linear regression, with gradient-noise covariance σ²H independent of the parameters, the stationary state is Gaussian with parameter covariance ησ²H(H + λI)⁻¹/(2S(1 − β)) and velocity covariance σ²H/(S(1 − β²)): for small weight decay it spreads equally along every nonzero Hessian direction and not along the null space, each Hessian eigenmode is a damped oscillator with damping ratio (1 − β)/√(2η(1 + β)(ρ + λ)), and the expected squared step is η²σ² tr(H)/(S(1 − β²)) *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-209](../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md) — A converged network trained with SGD is not at a point and does not sample its training loss: under a quadratic approximation it samples a Gibbs distribution on a modified loss, isotropic in the Hessian's column space, with probability currents that keep it oscillating, so its speed and spread are set by the learning rate, momentum and batch size *(Proposed)*

### From In the stochastic-differential-equation model of SGD, with a gradient-noise covariance that depends on the parameters, minibatch noise drives the difference of squared norms along a rescaling symmetry, at a rate proportional to learning rate over batch size, to the point on the symmetry orbit where the gradient-noise traces of the two parameter groups are equal, whenever both groups carry noise; so at stationarity SGD neither keeps the difference fixed, as gradient flow does, nor lets it diffuse, as isotropic noise does, and differs from gradient descent by a finite amount however small the noise

- [THEORY-211](../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md) — In the stochastic-differential-equation model of SGD, with a gradient-noise covariance that depends on the parameters, minibatch noise drives the difference of squared norms along a rescaling symmetry, at a rate proportional to learning rate over batch size, to the point on the symmetry orbit where the gradient-noise traces of the two parameter groups are equal, whenever both groups carry noise; so at stationarity SGD neither keeps the difference fixed, as gradient flow does, nor lets it diffuse, as isotropic noise does, and differs from gradient descent by a finite amount however small the noise *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-790](../record/theory.d/THEORY-790.md) — In deep networks trained by SGD on real data, minibatch noise drives parameter groups related by a rescaling symmetry toward the point where their gradient noise balances, at a rate set by learning rate over batch size, so that at stationarity they sit neither where gradient flow would leave them nor spread out as under isotropic noise, as Ziyin, Li and Ueda propose *(Proposed)*

### From For classical systems with Markovian, microscopically reversible dynamics, the entropy production of a trajectory obeys an exact finite-time symmetry against the time-reversed process, P_F(+ω)/P_R(−ω) = e^ω, wherever ω is odd under reversal; Jarzynski's work equality and the mean second law follow as corollaries, and the symmetry constrains fluctuations, not which steady state a system selects

- [THEORY-431](../record/theory.d/THEORY-431.md) — For classical systems with Markovian, microscopically reversible dynamics, the entropy production of a trajectory obeys an exact finite-time symmetry against the time-reversed process, P_F(+ω)/P_R(−ω) = e^ω, wherever ω is odd under reversal; Jarzynski's work equality and the mean second law follow as corollaries, and the symmetry constrains fluctuations, not which steady state a system selects *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-482](../record/theory.d/THEORY-482.md) — For a closed quantum system that starts thermal and is measured projectively in energy before and after a unitary drive, the two-point-measurement work obeys the Jarzynski equality and the Tasaki–Crooks relation in exactly the classical form, because those energy measurements erase the coherences in which a quantum difference could appear *(Active)*

## translation

### From In Goldwasser, Gruber, Kalai and Paradise's common-nonsense model, where the source language and the plausibility prior are uniform over sets from which shared random nonsense is removed and translators are one-to-one, maximum likelihood with the prior alone translates without parallel data with error O(log|Θ| / (α·min(m, |T|))) with high probability, falling in the shared nonsense α, in the size of the source language and in the number of samples

- [THEORY-270](../record/theory.d/THEORY-270.md) — In Goldwasser, Gruber, Kalai and Paradise's common-nonsense model, where the source language and the plausibility prior are uniform over sets from which shared random nonsense is removed and translators are one-to-one, maximum likelihood with the prior alone translates without parallel data with error O(log|Θ| / (α·min(m, |T|))) with high probability, falling in the shared nonsense α, in the size of the source language and in the number of samples *(Active)*
  - [THEORY-806](../record/theory.d/THEORY-806.md) — Translation without parallel data, as of an unknown animal communication system into a human language, is learnable from a plausibility prior over the target language alone, with error falling as the common ground between the languages grows and as the source language grows richer *(Proposed)*
